method: Three parallel primary-source research passes; Jev-assisted source ranking, candidate comparison and source-need alignment; host contract review; separately authored challenge cases with author labels withheld from the model. Not exhaustive or systematic literature review.
comparison: Compared against the existing 180 question/profile titles and nearest contracts. Related mechanisms are adapted applications, not global novelty claims.

pre_inference_clarifications.change: Aligned person-only criteria with instructions; specific praise of work is learning-directed.
Explicit incompatible mechanism takes precedence over a correct mechanism when both occur; unknown refers to unusable reference.
Explicit cross-stage denial takes conflicting_disclosure precedence; internal source contradiction remains unknown.
When a question both confirms known information and asks a genuinely new detail, choose new_information; confirmation-only is justified_confirmation only with an explicit reason.
pre_inference_clarifications.reason: independent contract review: mixed confirmation and new detail

pre_inference_clarifications.change: If correction instructions mix a compatible remedy with a remedy that conflicts with the field rule, choose misleading_correction.
pre_inference_clarifications.reason: independent contract review: mixed valid and invalid remedies

pre_inference_clarifications.change: If the proposed consequence broadens one explicit scope dimension while narrowing another, choose scope_broadened. Preserve all explicit target and duration limits.
pre_inference_clarifications.reason: independent contract review: cross-dimensional scope changes

pre_inference_clarifications.change: If a promise both overstates one capability and understates another, choose capability_overpromised.
pre_inference_clarifications.reason: independent contract review: mixed directional capability claims

pre_inference_clarifications.change: For a compound observation, relevant_missing takes precedence when at least one relevant fact is absent, even if other facts are already represented.

An explicitly conflicting incentive takes precedence over activity_proxy when both apply. Merely counting activity without demonstrating the outcome remains activity_proxy unless the supplied consequence explicitly rewards behavior contrary to the goal.

limitations: Eight task-authored candidates, not globally novel discoveries or proven educational interventions.
Sources establish education or communication needs, not Jev efficacy. The broad early Jev relevance rank treated them mostly as background, and that result is retained.
W3C supplemental design patterns are not themselves WCAG conformance requirements or automated compliance certification.
All fixtures are synthetic author-labeled examples; no learner or inbox data, disability inference, live classroom testing, or production adaptation.
Source-alignment advisory checking initially returned provider_http_529. Exactly one bounded recovery succeeded; original error retained.
HL01 is an extrapolation from retrieval practice guidance; Jev source-alignment confidence was lower (0.62) than the other candidates and does not independently validate the adaptation.
Nearest-existing comparison inspected titles for all 180 profiles and full questions for closest general alignment/directness mechanisms. Use-case distinctness does not imply a new AI primitive.
These candidates have not yet had their 24 fixtures run by this research agent; parent may perform live screening and independent verification.
Per-source exact quotations are limited to one excerpt of at most 15 words.

research_jev_receipts.interpretation: Mostly relevant background, not direct evidence for Jev efficacy; host retained source-backed needs without claiming more.

sources.evidence_summary: IES recommends retrieval practice, worked-example/problem alternation, linking concrete with abstract representations, and deep explanatory questions. These educational recommendations inspire question designs; they do not evaluate Jev.

W3C supplemental guidance recommends explaining jargon and uncommon or application-specific meanings. This motivates detecting an explicitly demonstrated vocabulary mismatch, without inferring disability or reading level.
W3C recommends nearby explanations for implied or ambiguous material, including metaphors. The proposed pattern checks supplied text only, not reader traits or emotional states.

EEF distinguishes feedback directed at work, subject processes, or self-regulation from general comments about a person's characteristics. It notes boundaries between productive categories can blur; the proposed question does not force those subcategories.
W3C recommends clear separated steps with necessary information included. The referent-ambiguity question is a task-authored specialization of this clarity need, not an explicit W3C test.

candidates.purpose: Check whether the material visible during a recall exercise already supplies its target answer.
candidates.distinctness: This concerns answer leakage in a human recall exercise, not whether software test assertions exist or cover a requirement.

candidates.purpose: Check that the omitted step of a worked example elicits the explicitly selected skill.
candidates.distinctness: Related to alignment checks, but the object is the cognitive work left to the learner by scaffolded examples, not test coverage or answer directness.

candidates.purpose: Check a concrete analogy against one explicitly stated abstract relationship.
candidates.distinctness: Targets relational transfer from abstract rule to concrete analogy, not whether a factual assertion is cited or an extracted value belongs to an entity.

candidates.purpose: Classify whether feedback offers task/process guidance or only a general judgment of the learner.
candidates.distinctness: Audits the target of educational feedback, independent of whether a response answers its question or fixes a prompt defect.

candidates.purpose: Detect an explicitly evidenced meaning mismatch around one term in a learning conversation.
candidates.distinctness: Word-sense negotiation is not entity alignment or deciding whether ambiguous actions share a safe next read.

candidates.purpose: Check whether a pronoun or vague noun identifies one object within an explicit local candidate set.
candidates.distinctness: Checks local instructional reference ambiguity before selection; H22 asks whether candidates cover the universe, and L13 aligns an entity mention.

candidates.purpose: Detect when an instruction depends on a metaphor or idiom without explaining the requested literal action.
candidates.distinctness: This audits reliance on unexplained nonliteral language, not an output fidelity contract or how directly a reply answers a question.

candidates.purpose: Separate a learner's stated why/how explanation from restating the observed result.
candidates.distinctness: Directness and citation checks can pass a repetition. This specifically checks whether a response articulates the requested explanatory relationship.

request.query: Find practical distinct semantic judgments that help people follow instructions, recover from service errors, and correct misunderstandings in AI interactions. Prioritize specific evidence relationships over generic style ratings.

candidates.text: GOV.UK Question pages: only ask users for information you really need; make clear why asking; allow 'I do not know' if valid; only ask a piece of information once in one journey; start with one question per page.
W3C Error Suggestion SC 3.3.3: If an input error is automatically detected and suggestions for correction are known, suggestions are provided unless this jeopardizes security or purpose.

Microsoft Research Human-AI interaction guidelines: make clear what system can do; support efficient dismissal and correction; scope services when in doubt; encourage granular feedback; convey consequences of user actions.
GOV.UK Check answers: show users a summary of their answers before submitting so they can check information and change answers.

candidates.title: Preserve the work the person wants to do
candidates.purpose: Check whether a proposed helper response takes over a part of the task the user explicitly reserved for themselves.
candidates.distinctness: H09 classifies whether work advances a goal; this asks who should perform a part that is already within the goal. A useful in-scope step can still take away explicitly retained authorship.

candidates.title: What is the user correcting?
candidates.purpose: Distinguish a factual correction, presentation preference, or changed objective in explicit feedback.
candidates.distinctness: L06 compares new evidence to a remembered fact; E05 compares requirement documents. This interprets a user's correction of a particular AI output before choosing an edit, without altering memory.

candidates.title: Does a recommendation disclose its tradeoff?
candidates.purpose: Check whether a recommendation acknowledges a stated downside that matters to the user's explicit priorities.
candidates.distinctness: H24 composes scores and vetoes, and H04 routes reviewer disagreements. This examines how a recommendation communicates an already-stated tradeoff, without selecting the winner or averaging preferences.

candidates.title: Surface human context absent from the AI packet
candidates.purpose: Identify whether a supplied user observation contains task-relevant context missing from the AI's current evidence packet.
candidates.distinctness: H10 reacts to evidence undermining a delivered recommendation. This acts before recommendation construction to identify a semantic information asymmetry; no contradiction or existing recommendation is required.

candidates.title: Does the success metric measure the user's outcome?
candidates.purpose: Distinguish an outcome measure from an activity proxy or an incentive that works against the explicit user goal.
candidates.distinctness: L05 checks whether success is stated; E02 checks a software test against a requirement. This assumes a goal and metric exist and identifies whether a human-facing productivity metric substitutes activity for the desired outcome.

candidates.title: Which explanation does the person need?
candidates.purpose: Identify the explicit target of a user's explanation request about an AI result.
candidates.distinctness: L19 classifies broad answer construction work; L22 checks answer directness. This distinguishes explanation targets within one work type so evidence, contrast, process and recovery are not conflated.

candidates.title: Are alternatives compared on the same basis?
candidates.purpose: Check a comparison draft for uneven criteria or mismatched evidence status across the alternatives the user named.
candidates.distinctness: H18 checks general evidence obligations and H24 scores candidates. This focuses on row/column parity and evidence-status symmetry in a human-readable comparison of explicitly supplied alternatives, not their merit.

candidates.title: Can the person resume after the AI stops?
candidates.purpose: Check whether an AI-to-human handoff explains the current state and a concrete next step.
candidates.distinctness: H03 preserves unresolved branches in agent handoff and BH47 checks unsupported completion claims. This checks whether an end-user can take over a partially completed task, including what to do next; it does not judge agent-memory completeness.
